subject: FastPay inference bottleneck profile + success metrics — next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Reed <olivia@fastpay.com>, Raj Patel <techlead@fastpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-27T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: FastPay inference bottleneck profile + success metrics — next steps

Hi Olivia / Raj — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed plan so we can move to a technical workshop next week.

What we heard (pain & impact)
- Real pain: intermittent spikes where customer-facing token-generation p95 for the chat feature degrades from ~120ms to 900–1,200ms under peak load, causing UI jank and timeouts.
- Business impact: checkout abandonment and a 6–8% drop in conversion during sustained peak traffic windows (10AM–12PM PST daily).
- Current mitigation: occasional synchronous fallback to a smaller model and conservative rate limiting — both reduce quality or throughput.

Your current stack
- Frontend: React app using streaming with SSE.
- Backend: Node + internal request broker; requests route to an in-house endpoint that proxies to a managed LLM service (quantized gpt-3.5-ish variant).
- Hosting: AWS us-west-2, autoscaling but with cold-start burst problems.

Quantitative targets you shared
- P95 target for token response latency: <= 250ms for interactive flows.
- Concurrent active sessions: 1,200–1,800 during peak (burst to 2,500+).
- Streaming experience: clients expect the first streamed token within ~80–100ms and steady per-token cadence without large pauses.

Immediate asks from our side
1) Share a 2-hour trace dump (sampled) covering a peak window if possible — will help us correlate queueing vs model decode time.
2) If available, export your per-request payload sizes and model config (batching settings, seq lengths).
3) Confirm whether KV-cache is preserved across your proxy (yes/no).

Attachments: latency-snapshot.csv (small sample we took from our observability notes for benchmarking).

Proposed next steps
- Technical workshop: 60–75 min deep dive — focus on request routing, batching opportunities, and streaming cadence. Suggest slots: Wed 3/3 10:00–11:15 PT or Thu 3/4 13:00–14:15 PT.
- Pre-work: you send traces + sample requests; we’ll run a quick local repro and bring a concise experiment plan (quantization, batching, and prefix cache options).
- Goal for the workshop: arrive at a focused 2-week trial plan that targets p95 <=250ms for chat and stable streaming UX at 2k concurrency.

If that aligns, I’ll book the workshop and loop in an engineer from our runtime team for the deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0192

Date: 2027-02-27T17:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastPay inference bottleneck profile + success metrics — next steps

Thanks Evelyn — this is great, and captures the issues well. A few clarifications from our end:

- The 900–1,200ms p95 spikes are observed primarily when sequence lengths exceed ~420 tokens (ticket threads + context). Outside those windows we’re closer to 180–220ms p95.
- Our proxy currently preserves KV-cache for the same session, but cache warmup is inconsistent after autoscale events.
- We can share traces — attaching a 30MB sampled traces bundle and a short CSV of request sizes.

Attachments: fastpay-traces.zip (30MB), requests-agg.csv (12KB)

Wed 3/3 10:00 PT works for us for the workshop. Please include an engineer who can speak to batching/quantization tradeoffs — Raj will be present from our side.

Olivia
Director, Product — FastPay
olivia@fastpay.com
